subagent_reports.topic: Discovery opportunity scout for Epic retirement lifecycle

sources.label: epic-state.ts applyEpicArchivedToState (no guard)
sources.summary: applyEpicArchivedToState unconditionally sets state.status='archived' and progress.status='archived' with NO precondition — does not require completed status or check for active/in-flight entries. Contrast with applyEpicMergedToState (line 700-728) which rejects with code 'epic_not_active' when progress.status==='completed'. Retirement path can archive an in-flight Epic, violating proposal Must-Not 'Must not silently delete/hide active initiative state without typed transition'.

sources.label: epicArchivedSignal has no tool caller
sources.summary: epicArchivedSignal is wired only in workflows.ts:1925-1930 handler and referenced in tests. Store epics.ts imports epicMergedSignal but NOT epicArchivedSignal; no store archive()/retire() method exists. No adv_epic_archive or adv_epic_retire tool in epicTools. The archived transition is dead code from a public-surface view — reachable only via internal signal, never fired by any user path.

sources.label: recomputeEpicProgress completed vs workflow status divergence
sources.summary: recomputeEpicProgress derives progress.status='completed' when completed===total>0, but state.status (workflow lifecycle) stays 'active' until epicArchivedSignal. workflows.ts:1934-1948 only completes the workflow execution when state.status==='archived'. Completed Epics keep their workflow running indefinitely — root cause of the leak described in the proposal.

sources.label: list-epic-workflows.ts enumerates all by type, no status filter
sources.summary: buildEpicVisibilityQuery returns only WorkflowType='epicWorkflow'; listEpicWorkflowIds filters by project prefix in-process. No ExecutionStatus or status attribute filter. Because completed Epics never complete their workflow (finding above), a Visibility ExecutionStatus filter alone would NOT hide completed-but-running Epics — the fix must make completion terminate the workflow AND/OR filter progress.status.

sources.label: adv_epic_list returns unfiltered epics.list()
sources.summary: adv_epic_list description claims 'List all active Epics' but execute calls owner.store.epics.list() then paginates with no progress.status filter. store list() queries every enumerated Epic workflow and sorts by created_at. Description/behavior mismatch: it lists ALL Epics regardless of terminal status.

sources.label: rq-epicMerge01 reference model for typed audited terminal transition
sources.summary: Merge is the by-the-book precedent: typed, audited, plan-first mutation with evidence + expected_version optimistic concurrency, terminal-source rejection, dryRun preview, and 'source Epic left readable with pointer and no active next-work'. adv_epic_merge args (evidence, expected_*_version, dryRun, target routing) are a directly reusable contract shape for a retirement tool.

sources.label: rq-epicCliList01 constrains CLI to read-only, no hydration
sources.summary: rq-epicCliList01.4 requires the Epic CLI namespace remain read-only and MUST NOT dispatch archive/mutation verbs, and the list path MUST NOT query/hydrate per-Epic workflow. Any active-only CLI filtering must come from Visibility ExecutionStatus (structural), not per-Epic progress hydration. This bounds the design: retirement must terminate the workflow so ExecutionStatus becomes a valid CLI-safe filter.

sources.label: rq-epicArchiveSync01 + rq-epicOptionalMembership01 already handle child-archive & orphaning
sources.summary: rq-epicOptionalMembership01.body explicitly states 'changes whose Epic is later archived MUST remain valid and continue through the normal gate/task flow'. So orphaned-child handling on Epic retirement is already a spec law and does not need new invention — but the retirement tool must not break it (no child hard-block).

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: The state model already distinguishes completed (progress projection) from archived (workflow lifecycle), and an archived transition + signal + pure state helper already exist. The real gaps are (1) NO public tool fires epicArchivedSignal, so retirement is unreachable; (2) completed Epics never terminate their Temporal workflow, so they leak into Visibility enumeration and adv_epic_list; (3) applyEpicArchivedToState has no precondition guard, unlike the merge path, risking archival of in-flight Epics; (4) adv_epic_list claims 'active' but does not filter. The merge feature (rq-epicMerge01 / adv_epic_merge) is a strong, in-repo, by-the-book reference for a typed, audited, plan-first, version-checked, dryRun-capable terminal transition — retirement should mirror it rather than invent a new pattern. CLI active-only filtering is constrained by rq-epicCliList01 to Visibility ExecutionStatus (no per-Epic hydration), which structurally requires completion to actually terminate the workflow.

validation.notes: No hard blockers to the scoped discovery objective. Caution flags: (1) the unguarded applyEpicArchivedToState is a real safety gap the design must close (guard on completed/no-active-entries or require explicit force+evidence); (2) whether completion should auto-terminate the workflow vs require explicit retirement is a genuine policy fork that changes both Visibility filtering feasibility and CLI semantics — this is a user-surface decision, not auto-adoptable. Confidence medium because the auto-vs-explicit retirement policy is deferred to discovery per the proposal and materially affects the design.

tradeoffs: Auto-retire-on-completed: zero operator action and immediate leak fix, but removes the human/audit checkpoint and makes 'completed but I still want it visible for planning' impossible without a re-open path.

Explicit typed retirement (mirror adv_epic_merge): auditable, evidence-bearing, reversible-by-design, but leaves completed Epics leaking until an operator acts — does not by itself fix the enumeration leak.

Hybrid (completed is a distinct progress status; retirement is a separate audited transition that terminates the workflow): cleanest separation and matches existing completed/archived split, but is the largest surface (new tool + store method + Visibility filter + CLI + spec laws).

Reusing epicArchivedSignal vs adding an epicRetiredSignal: reusing avoids replay/history churn and new schema, but 'archived' currently has no guard and its semantics may need to widen; a dedicated retired status/signal is clearer but adds an enum value and migration surface.

alternatives_considered.option: Consumer-side filtering only (each surface hides completed Epics)
alternatives_considered.rationale: Directly violates proposal Must-Not 'Must not rely on each consumer to infer whether a completed Epic is inactive' and rq-epicCliList01's no-hydration constraint would force per-Epic progress reads the CLI is forbidden from doing.

alternatives_considered.option: Reuse existing epicArchivedSignal + add a guarded adv_epic_retire tool mirroring adv_epic_merge contract
alternatives_considered.rationale: Minimal new surface, reuses proven typed/audited/version-checked/dryRun pattern, and the missing tool is the actual gap. Requires adding a precondition guard to applyEpicArchivedToState (or a wrapper) so only completed/terminal Epics retire without explicit force.

Cleanly fixes the Visibility/CLI leak and enables ExecutionStatus filtering, but is a policy decision (loss of a checkpoint, reopen semantics) that the proposal explicitly defers to discovery and the user must arbitrate.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Design a typed, audited adv_epic_retire tool modeled on adv_epic_merge (evidence + expected_version + dryRun + owner routing), add a precondition guard to the archived transition so non-completed Epics require explicit force+evidence, and make retirement actually terminate the Epic workflow so rq-epicCliList01-compliant Visibility ExecutionStatus filtering becomes viable. Surface the auto-retire-on-completed vs explicit-retirement policy fork to the user before locking the agreement.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Adopt now (auto-adopt, low-risk, evidence-backed): (1) close the applyEpicArchivedToState guard gap; (2) fix the adv_epic_list description/behavior mismatch; (3) reuse the adv_epic_merge contract shape for the new retirement tool. Surface to user (policy fork): auto-retire-on-completed vs explicit operator retirement vs hybrid — this changes workflow-termination and CLI-filter design and is deferred by the proposal. Defer: any launcher/toolbox cross-project shape changes until a concrete external consumer requirement is proven.
follow_ups: Confirm with orchestrator/user whether completed Epics auto-terminate their Temporal workflow (enables Visibility ExecutionStatus filter) or require explicit retirement.
Design must add a precondition guard on the archived transition (completed/no-active-entries) or an explicit force+evidence escape hatch, matching the merge path's terminal-source rejection.
Verify rq-epicOptionalMembership01 (orphaned-child-on-archive) stays green: retirement must not hard-block or invalidate in-flight child changes.

sources.label: epic-state.ts merge-guard vs unguarded archive (in-repo)
sources.summary: isClosedForMutation() + closedForMutationFailure() + epic_not_active check exist and are used by all 12 mutation helpers AND applyEpicMergedToState. But applyEpicArchivedToState (731-741) is UNGUARDED (no completed/merged/archived rejection). Design Decision 3 guard can reuse the exact merge-guard pattern instead of a new helper.

sources.label: store epics.ts list hydration + no retire method + no retired projection (in-repo)
sources.summary: Store.epics.list() hydrates every Epic via queryEpic (DDC1 no-hydration gap is real). No retire/archive store method exists. No retired-history disk projection exists anywhere in storage/. Confirms Decision 5 (retired projection) and DDC2 are genuinely net-new, not redundant. Epic store passes searchAttributesEnabled:false.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Draft design is architecturally sound and correctly reuses the signal-driven epic workflow, isClosedForMutation guard family, and expected-version/dry-run merge pattern. Two candidates are strong auto-adopt simplifications: (1) the guarded-archive transition should reuse the existing applyEpicMergedToState guard pattern rather than a 'new pure helper', and (2) active-only listing (pillar 4 / Decision 4 / DDC5) can be built on the BUILT-IN Temporal `ExecutionStatus = "Running"` filter — which the codebase already uses in lifecycle-visibility.ts and Temporal docs confirm — because the epic workflow terminates on archive. This removes the proposed custom `AdvEpicStatus` search-attribute registration, its reconnect/repair tests, and an entire risk category, while satisfying C2/AC3/AC5/DDC1/DDC5. Decision 5 (retired disk projection) and DDC2 remain genuinely necessary: no retired-epic projection exists today and a completed workflow cannot be queried, so this is the real net-new work and the correct place to spend design effort. One overlooked ordering risk: DDC3/DDC4 require projection-before-signal AND rejection-before-projection; because archive completes the workflow, the retire store method cannot re-query live state after signaling (workflow gone), so idempotency/reconcile must read the retired projection, not the live workflow.

validation.notes: No contract compromise or release blocker. Caution (not pass) because the design over-scopes with a custom AdvEpicStatus search attribute that the built-in ExecutionStatus filter makes unnecessary for the active/retired distinction — adopting the simpler path reduces registration risk and test surface. This is a simplification recommendation surfaced for orchestrator/design synthesis, not a defect that fails the design.

tradeoffs: ExecutionStatus-only active filtering cannot distinguish retired-vs-merged-vs-error terminal states in one Visibility query; if a future consumer needs terminal-reason faceting, a custom attribute or projection read is still required. For AC3/AC5 (active-only) this is not needed now.

Reusing applyEpicMergedToState's guard means archive/retire inherits its 'completed required' semantics; retirement wants the OPPOSITE completed-required rule vs merge's completed-forbidden rule, so the guard must be adapted (allow completed, reject active/merged/archived), not copied verbatim.
Retired disk projection adds a new external-state artifact to own and test, but it is unavoidable given completed-workflow un-queryability (DDC2).

alternatives_considered.option: Add custom AdvEpicStatus Keyword search attribute (as drafted, pillar 4/Decision 4/DDC5)
alternatives_considered.rationale: Redundant for active/retired: epic workflow terminates on archive so built-in ExecutionStatus = 'Running' already yields active-only listing with zero registration. Adds fail-closed registration/reconnect/repair risk and test surface for no required capability.

alternatives_considered.option: New standalone guard helper for archive transition
alternatives_considered.rationale: isClosedForMutation + epic_not_active + checkVersion + checkIdempotency already exist and are the established pattern; a new helper duplicates them. Adapt the transition to require completed and reuse existing guards.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep retired history in live workflow (no projection)
alternatives_considered.rationale: Archive completes the workflow (workflows.ts:1934-1948); a completed workflow cannot be queried, so DDC2/AC4 history-by-ID would break. Projection is required.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Adopt two simplifications during design finalization: (A) drop custom AdvEpicStatus; implement active-only Epic listing via WorkflowType = epicWorkflow AND ExecutionStatus = 'Running' (extend listEpicWorkflowIds with a statuses/activeOnly option, keep prefix filter), and route store.epics.list default through it with no per-Epic hydration; (B) implement the guarded archive as an adaptation of applyEpicMergedToState (require progress.status === completed, reject active entries/merged/archived, expected-version, idempotency) rather than a new helper. Keep Decision 5 retired projection as the primary net-new work, and require the retire store method to reconcile idempotency via the projection (not live workflow re-query) since the workflow is gone post-archive.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Auto-adopt candidates 1 (ExecutionStatus-based active listing, drop AdvEpicStatus) and 2 (reuse/adapt merge guard). User-surface candidate 3 (retired projection ordering + post-archive reconcile-via-projection) for design confirmation. Candidates 4-5 are low-cost confirmations.
follow_ups: Design should state explicitly that the retire store method reads the retired projection (not the completed workflow) for idempotency/already-retired responses, since applyEpicArchivedToState completion makes live re-query impossible.
Confirm merge-guard adaptation direction: merge forbids completed sources; retire REQUIRES completed — same guard scaffolding, inverted status precondition.

The central risk it targets is real: firing epicArchivedSignal drives epicWorkflow to a completing state (workflows.ts:1934-1947), after which live state queries throw WorkflowNotFound and return null (epics.ts:90-106). A durable retired projection written BEFORE workflow completion (DDC3) is genuinely required to satisfy AC4/C1 history access; this is not over-engineering. DDC1 (default listing via ExecutionStatus=Running + workflow-ID prefix, no per-Epic hydration) is directly mandated by rq-epicCliList01 and already implemented for changes/members, so it is feasible with existing Visibility infrastructure. The live-first-then-projection read for adv_epic_show mirrors the existing rq-replayFallback01 temporal_query_fallback pattern used for changes: a reuse, not a novel mechanism. Key Decisions 2 (keep internal status archived, expose retirement wording) and 4 (no custom AdvEpicStatus) are the boring, minimal choices and are preferred correctly in LBP. Notable asymmetry the design leverages: merge keeps the workflow running while archive completes it, which is exactly why retirement (=archived terminal) mandates the projection that merge did not. Gap: design.md does not name the concrete durable projection mechanism (disk projection vs memo vs Visibility memo) or the precise adv_epic_show fallback resolution, and the store has no existing markArchived/retire method or retired-projection writer to extend. This is a design-completeness caution to resolve in planning, not a correctness blocker. Spec-law: no advance-epics requirement is contradicted; a new rq-epicRetire01-style requirement should make the completed-only guard, projection-before-completion invariant, active-only default listing, and retired-history read executable law (agreement objective 6, constraint C2). AC5 warrant spec:rq-epicCliList01 is satisfied by DDC1.

validation.notes: Design solves all objectives and is spec-compliant (rq-epicCliList01, rq-epicMerge01, rq-epicArchiveSync01, rq-epicTerminalChildProjection01, C5/AC2 guard). The projection-before-completion invariant is verified against workflows.ts:1934-1947 and epics.ts:90-106. Single caution: design.md leaves the durable retired-projection persistence mechanism and adv_epic_show fallback-read resolution unspecified, and no store archive/retire method or projection writer exists yet to extend. Recommend naming the projection store (align with the existing disk-projection + memo pattern used by changes / rq-replayFallback01) and the exact live-then-projection read order as a Design-Derived Criterion before the planning gate. Also recommend an explicit ordering test proving projection write precedes epicArchivedSignal (DDC3) and an idempotency/retry test for projection-written-but-signal-failed (DDC5), since the workflow becomes unqueryable post-completion.

## Why

ADV Epics can become `completed` when all entries are terminal, but completed Epic workflows can remain visible indefinitely in Temporal and can leak into external launcher/planning surfaces unless each consumer filters them. ADV needs an owning lifecycle/retirement mechanism for completed Epics rather than relying only on consumers to hide them.

## Cross-Project Origin

This change was created as a follow-up from **toolbox**.

|-------|-------|
| Source project | toolbox |
| Source path | `/home/jon/toolbox` |
| Validation | `git -C /home/jon/toolbox rev-parse --show-toplevel` returned `/home/jon/toolbox`; source path is a Git project |
| User confirmation | User selected `Yes, valid` during discovery |

## What Changes

Define and implement a first-class Epic retirement path for completed Epics. Discovery selected explicit operator retirement, with manual dry-run/backfill support for existing completed Epics and active-only default CLI/list semantics.

## User Outcomes

- Active Epic and next-work surfaces show only Epics that can still guide work.
- Completed Epics have an owned path out of active enumeration.
- Retired Epic history remains available for audit and troubleshooting.
- Active initiative state is not deleted or hidden without a typed lifecycle transition.

## Scope

### In Scope

- Epic lifecycle/status semantics for completed versus retired/archived Epics.
- Temporal Visibility-backed Epic listing behavior and active-planning enumeration semantics.
- Explicit typed Epic retirement/archive surface with dry-run and audit evidence.
- Audit/history access for retired Epics through typed reads.
- Manual dry-run/report path for existing completed Epics.
- Tests for completed Epic retirement, active listing exclusion, and retained history access.
- Spec updates for `advance-epics` lifecycle and listing requirements.

### Out of Scope

- Making Epic membership mandatory for all ADV changes.
- Adding Jira-like ownership, sprint, estimate, board, or assignment primitives.
- Deleting Epic history or removing audit access to retired Epics.
- Rewriting change archive/release semantics except where Epic entry terminal projection needs integration evidence.
- Product-wide launcher changes outside the current Advance plugin unless a concrete downstream consumer requirement is proven.

### Must Not

- Must not rely on each consumer to infer whether a completed Epic is inactive.
- Must not silently delete completed Epics or make history inaccessible.
- Must not retire an active/incomplete Epic.
- Must not hard-block normal change gates solely because Epic order is advisory or incomplete.
- Must not mutate ADV state files directly; Epic lifecycle changes must use typed tools/signals/state.

# Design

## Architecture Overview

Add explicit Epic retirement as a typed lifecycle transition for completed Epics. Retirement is operator-triggered, audited, expected-version guarded, and dry-run-capable. Internally it reuses the existing archived terminal workflow state, while the public user-facing tool presents the action as retirement.

Architecture pillars:

1. Epic workflow state remains source of truth while the workflow is running.
2. Retirement preflight proves the Epic is completed and has no active/future entries before any mutation.
3. Retirement persists a durable retired-Epic projection before completing the workflow so `adv_epic_show` can read retired history after the Temporal workflow is no longer queryable.
4. Active/default list surfaces use Temporal `ExecutionStatus = "Running"` plus workflow type/project-prefix filtering to exclude retired workflows without hydrating every Epic for CLI.
5. Completed-but-unretired Epics remain running until explicit retirement. They may appear in owner/operator surfaces as retirement candidates, not as next-work entries.

## Key Decisions

### 1. Public lifecycle tool: `adv_epic_retire`

Add an Epic owner-scoped tool with the same routing/trust shape as other owner-only Epic tools.

Inputs:

- `epic_id`
- `expected_version`
- `evidence` (required audit evidence)
- `retired_by` optional, default `agent`
- `dryRun` optional
- `epic_owner_target_path` / trust confirmation fields

Dry-run returns current status/progress/version, eligibility, blockers, projected retired summary, and whether a retired projection already exists.

Execution order:

1. Query current Epic workflow state.
2. Reject before mutation unless `progress.status === "completed"` and every entry is terminal.
3. Persist retired projection with evidence and actor through the storage layer.
4. Signal `epicArchivedSignal` to set archived state and allow workflow completion.
5. Return projection-backed retired summary, not a post-signal live workflow query.

### 2. Use existing archive state; expose retirement semantics at tool layer

Keep internal Epic status vocabulary as `archived` for compatibility with existing schema, workflow, and tests. The user-facing tool and docs call the operator action retirement. Avoid a schema-wide `retired` rename in this change.

### 3. Guard archive/retire with existing mutation scaffolding

Adapt existing Epic mutation patterns instead of adding unrelated machinery:

- Reuse version/idempotency/rejection patterns already present around Epic merge/update.
- Invert merge's completed-source guard: merge forbids completed source Epics, retirement requires completed source Epics.
- Update the pure state transition so the archived signal cannot archive active/incomplete Epics.
- Tool preflight still checks blockers first so normal failures produce actionable tool output before any signal.

### 4. Use built-in Temporal execution status for active/default listing

Do not add a custom `AdvEpicStatus` search attribute for this change. The retired workflow completes after archival, so `ExecutionStatus = "Running"` structurally excludes retired Epics from default CLI/list enumeration without registration drift.

Design impact:

- `listEpicWorkflowIds` gains an option for active/default running-only enumeration.
- Default CLI `adv epic list --json` uses `WorkflowType = "epicWorkflow" AND ExecutionStatus = "Running"`, then keeps existing project-prefix filtering.
- MCP `adv_epic_list` defaults to running/non-retired Epics; it may hydrate returned running Epics for rich output.
- Completed-but-unretired Epics remain running and visible to operators until retired; this honors explicit-retire policy.

### 5. Retired history projection is required

Temporal queries cannot be relied on after the Epic workflow completes. Retirement therefore writes a storage-owned projection before signaling workflow completion.

Projection location/owner:

- Add an Epic-retirement projection surface owned by the storage layer beside existing ADV external state paths, e.g. under an Epic archive/retired directory managed from `store.paths` or a dedicated typed helper.
- The projection writer/reader must be internal storage/tool code; agents never read or mutate these files directly.
- Align implementation style with change-side live-query→durable projection fallback, but keep the Epic projection intentionally smaller than change archive bundles.

Projection fields:

- Epic record snapshot
- `retired_at`
- `retired_by`
- `evidence`
- source workflow ID
- source version
- projection status metadata (`prepared` or `retired`) for retry reconciliation

`adv_epic_show` read order:

1. Try live workflow query first.
2. If workflow is not found/completed/unqueryable, load retired projection by Epic ID.
3. Return the same compact/full shapes, with retirement metadata included.
4. If both live workflow and projection are missing, return typed `EPIC_NOT_FOUND`/read error as today.

### 6. Manual completed-candidate report

Add a non-mutating completed-candidate path through `adv_epic_list` status/mode support or a dedicated candidate helper. Preferred shape for prep: extend `adv_epic_list` with a status filter such as `status: "active" | "completed" | "archived" | "merged" | "all"`, defaulting to active/running. `status: "completed"` hydrates running Epics and reports completed-unretired candidates without mutation.

No automatic bulk retirement/backfill is added.

## ADR Drafts

No ADR required. Decisions are meaningful but not hard-to-reverse enough to justify an ADR: tool naming, projection placement, and list filtering can evolve through typed tools/specs without permanent architectural lock-in.

## Implementation Strategy

1. **Spec law**
   - Add `advance-epics` requirements for explicit retirement, active-retire guard, active/default list semantics, dry-run/candidate report, and retired-history readback.
   - Update docs mirror.

2. **Types and store contracts**
   - Add retired projection type near Epic storage/types.
   - Extend `Store.epics` with `retire(...)` and list options.
   - Add disk-store stubs that fail with Temporal-required errors for mutating Epic retirement.

3. **Workflow and pure state**
   - Modify `applyEpicArchivedToState` to reject non-completed states or replace it with a guarded mutation result helper.
   - Preserve existing workflow completion condition `state.status === "archived"`.
   - Add tests for active/incomplete archive rejection, completed archive success, already-archived behavior, and workflow completion after retire.

4. **Storage projection**
   - Implement retired projection write/read in storage layer, not via direct agent file edits.
   - Write projection before archive signal; if signal fails, retry reconciles by querying live workflow first and using projection metadata.
   - `adv_epic_show` falls back to projection when live query cannot return retired state.

5. **List surfaces**
   - Update `listEpicWorkflowIds` to accept active/running-only mode and include `ExecutionStatus = "Running"` in default active query.
   - Update `store.epics.list` to support default running list plus status-filtered completed/all modes for MCP.
   - Update `adv_epic_list` args/description/output so default means non-retired/running, and completed-candidate report is explicit.
   - Update `bin/lib/epic-list.ts` tests so CLI remains live, worker-free, and no-hydration.

6. **Tool surface**
   - Add `adv_epic_retire` with dry-run, evidence, expected version, and owner routing.
   - Use target-path trust preflight for remote owner mutation.
   - Return typed errors: `EPIC_NOT_FOUND`, `STALE_VERSION`, `EPIC_RETIRE_NOT_COMPLETED`, `EPIC_ALREADY_RETIRED`, `TARGET_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`, and projection/signal failure classes.

7. **Verification**
   - Add TDD tests for tool, storage, workflow, CLI, and spec mirror.
   - Include explicit tests for projection-before-signal ordering and projection-written/signal-failed retry reconciliation.
   - Run targeted Epic/CLI/spec tests, schema checks if public schemas change, then smoke/check suite per repo policy.

## LBP Analysis

Preferred approach: explicit retirement + built-in Temporal execution-status filtering + retired projection.

Why this is long-term better:

- Structural correctness: lifecycle is owned by typed tools, workflow guards, storage projection, and tests.
- No consumer heuristics: default list filtering is centralized in list/query helpers.
- No new search-attribute migration: `ExecutionStatus` is built into Temporal and already used elsewhere in ADV active-owner queries.
- Audit safety: user-selected explicit retire requires evidence and expected version.
- History safety: projection keeps retired state queryable after workflow completion.

Rejected alternatives:

- Consumer-side filtering: rejected because every caller would need to infer completion/retirement independently.
- Auto-retire on completion: rejected by user; hides state without operator action.
- Keep archived workflows running forever: rejected because it does not address Temporal active-work noise.
- Custom `AdvEpicStatus` search attribute: rejected as unnecessary for active/retired distinction and adds registration/repair drift.

## Affected Components

- `.adv/specs/advance-epics/spec.json`
- `docs/specs/advance-epics.md`
- `plugin/src/types/epics.ts`
- `plugin/src/types/signals.ts` if payload gains expected version/idempotency fields
- `plugin/src/storage/store-types.ts`
- `plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/epics.ts`
- `plugin/src/storage/store-disk.ts`
- storage path/projection helper modules for retired Epic projection
- `plugin/src/temporal/epic-state.ts`
- `plugin/src/temporal/workflows.ts`
- `plugin/src/temporal/list-epic-workflows.ts`
- `plugin/src/tools/epic.ts`
- `bin/lib/epic-list.ts`
- Epic/tool/CLI/spec tests near those files

## Design-Derived Criteria

- DDC1: CLI default Epic listing must remain no-hydration: it may use Temporal Visibility `ExecutionStatus = "Running"` and workflow ID prefix filtering, but must not query each Epic workflow.
- DDC2: Retired Epic history must not depend on querying a completed Temporal workflow.
- DDC3: Retirement execution must persist a history projection before signaling workflow completion, or otherwise prove no history-loss window.
- DDC4: Active/incomplete retirement rejection must happen before projection write or archive signal.
- DDC5: Retry/idempotency must reconcile projection-written/signal-failed cases by querying live workflow first, then projection metadata.
- DDC6: Completed-unretired Epics remain running until explicit retirement; any list/candidate semantics must label them structurally as completed candidates, not active next-work.
- DDC7: `adv_epic_show` fallback order is live workflow query first, retired projection second, typed not-found/error third.

## Risks / Mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Projection write then archive signal failure leaves projection for still-running Epic | Include projection status metadata; retry queries live workflow first and either completes signal or reports repairable prepared projection. |
| Post-signal live query impossible | Return retired result from projection and test `adv_epic_show` fallback. |
| CLI default behavior changes downstream expectations | User selected active-only; update spec/docs/tests and keep future history flag out of scope unless needed. |
| Completed-unretired Epics still appear in running Visibility | Treat explicit retirement as operator-controlled lifecycle; default rich MCP output labels `completed` and candidate mode lists them for retirement. |
| Guard only in tool layer could be bypassed by direct signal | Guard the pure state transition as well as tool/store preflight. |
| Remote Epic owner routing omitted | Reuse existing Epic owner routing schema in `adv_epic_retire` and tests. |

## Design Leverage Scout

- Candidates considered: 5.
- Auto-adopted: 4.
  - Dropped custom `AdvEpicStatus`; use built-in `ExecutionStatus = "Running"`.
  - Adapt existing Epic mutation/merge guard scaffolding instead of inventing new machinery.
  - Keep retired projection as the necessary net-new history store.
  - Route default list through no-hydration running workflow enumeration where CLI requires it.
- Surfaced/agent-resolved: 1.
  - Post-archive reconciliation must use retired projection, not live workflow re-query. This is technical, contract-tied, and incorporated as DDC2/DDC3/DDC5/DDC7.
- Inconclusive/skipped: none.

## Validation Summary

Validator result: caution, no blockers.

- Independent validator confirmed the history-loss window is real because Epic workflow completes when `status === "archived"`; projection-before-completion is required.
- Validator confirmed merge/archive asymmetry: merged sources keep workflows running, archived sources terminate, so retired projection is necessary where merge did not need one.
- Validator confirmed live-query to durable-projection fallback is an existing ADV pattern, not novel architecture.
- Validator confirmed `ExecutionStatus = "Running"` no-hydration listing aligns with existing ADV active-owner Visibility patterns and `rq-epicCliList01` constraints.
- Validator caution: design needed to name the retired-projection write/read path and exact `adv_epic_show` live-to-projection fallback order. This revision records both in Key Decision 5 and DDC7.

Validation disposition: proceed to planning. Add planning tasks for `rq-epicRetire01` spec law, projection-before-signal ordering test, and projection-written/signal-failed retry reconciliation test.
